Source heading includes ichthyoplankton despite separate fish-larvae group; preserve overlap caveat. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 10.2 pp108–109; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.]

Large crabs; detailed benthic composition and abundance observations are in chapter11/Table11.8. No exhaustive species list asserted by this summary. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 11 pp110–132; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.] Main contributing taxa in Table11.8 printed pp116–118: Liocarcinus holsatus; Hyas coarctatus; Cancer pagurus; Liocarcinus marmoreus; Pisidia longicornis; Lithodes maia. These are reported principal biomass contributors, not an exhaustive inventory.
Nephrops norvegicus. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 11 pp110–132; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.]

Free-living surface macrobenthos; mostly echinoderms, small crabs, gastropods and scallops [Table11.6 p115]. Epifaunal macrobenthos, mobile grazers; group is organised by benthic habit and size, not a single taxon. Taxon-specific benthic survey observations retained in Table11.8 evidence. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 11 pp110–132; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.] Main contributing taxa in Table11.8 printed pp116–118: Euspira pulchellus; Leptochiton asellus; Philine quadrata; Ophiura albida; OPHIUROIDEA; Euspira montagui; Hyala vitrea; Ophiura affinis; Anomia ephippium; Corystes cassivelaunus; Asterias rubens; Leptochiton. These are reported principal biomass contributors, not an exhaustive inventory.

Bivalves and gastropods mostly >2mm, filter feeders and grazers [Table11.6 printed p115; PDF117]. Infaunal macrobenthos; group is organised by benthic habit and size. Detailed survey species data are retained in Table11.8 evidence. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 11 pp110–132; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.] Main contributing taxa in Table11.8 printed pp116–118: Amphiura filiformis; Arctica islandica; Aphrodita aculeata; Mysella bidentata; NEMERTEA; Spisula subtruncata; Thyasira spp.; Chamelea gallina; Echinocardium cordatum; Abra prismatica; Gari fervensis; Echinocardium flavescens; Dosinia lupinus; Antalis entalis; Nicomache spp.; CAUDOFOVEATA; Nuculoma tenuis; Phaxas pellucidus; PELECYPODA. These are reported principal biomass contributors, not an exhaustive inventory.

Shrimp, benthic crustacean group; detailed survey composition retained in chapter11. Not all Crustacea. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 11 pp110–132; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.] Main contributing taxa in Table11.8 printed pp116–118: Crangon crangon; Crangon allmanni; Eualus pusiolus; Pandalus montagui; Spirontocaris lilljeborgi; Processa nouveli; Pandalus borealis; Pandalina spp.. These are reported principal biomass contributors, not an exhaustive inventory.

Crustaceans, molluscs and polychaetes at benthic interface plus mysids, gammarids and amphipods swarming off bottom [Table11.6 p115]. Small mobile epifauna (swarming crustaceans), separate from large epifaunal grazers and shrimp. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 11 pp110–132; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.] Main contributing taxa in Table11.8 printed pp116–118: Bathyporeia elegans; Harpinia antennaria; Urothoe poseidonis; Eudorellopsis deformis; Bathyporeia guilliamsoniana; Philine scabra; Eudorella emarginata. These are reported principal biomass contributors, not an exhaustive inventory.

Mostly polychaetes and small sediment-dwelling crustaceans; filter feeders and predators [Table11.6 printed p115]. Small infauna, principally polychaetes; size/habitat group. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 11 pp110–132; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.] Main contributing taxa in Table11.8 printed pp116–118: Myriochele spp.; Nephtys cirrosa; Ophelia borealis; Nephtys hombergii; Magelona spp.; Pholoe spp.; Phoronis spp.; Gattyana cirrosa; Minuspio cirrifera; Nephtys longosetosa; Goniada maculata; Levinsenia gracilis; Pisione remota; Exogone verugera; Amphictene auricoma; Spio filicornis; Aonides paucibranchiata; Owenia fusiformis; Exogone hebes; Notomastus latericeus; Paramphinome; Protodorvillea kefersteini; Lumbrineris latreilli; Caulleriella spp.; Goniadella bobretzkii; Diplocirrus glaucus; Nephtys caeca; Prionospio malmgreni; Pseudopolydora cf. pauchibranchiata; Tharyx spp.; Scalibregma inflatum; Poecilochaetus serpens; Anobothrus gracilis; Nephtys paradoxa; Glycinde nordmanni; Sthenelais limicola; Laonice sarsi; Scoloplos armiger. These are reported principal biomass contributors, not an exhaustive inventory.

Suspension/filter feeders including anemones, sponges, corals, tunicates, gorgonians, hydroids, anthozoans, pelecypods, barnacles, bryozoans, attached bivalves, crinoids, ascidians and oysters [Table11.6 p115]. Sessile epifauna, benthic habitat group; detailed survey composition retained in Table11.8 evidence. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 11 pp110–132; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.] Main contributing taxa in Table11.8 printed pp116–118: Sabellidae; Modiolus modiolus; Chaetopterus variopedatus; Serpulidae; Musculus discors; Modiolus barbatus; Musculus niger; Pododesmus patelliformis; Modiolus spp.; Serpula vermicularis; Sabellaria spinulosa. These are reported principal biomass contributors, not an exhaustive inventory.

Meiofauna, size class including nematodes and copepods discussed in chapter11; not interchangeable with pelagic copepods. [Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, 11 pp110–132; printed page, PDF page=printed+2. Source spellings preserved, nomenclature not independently reconciled.] Main contributing taxa in Table11.8 printed pp116–118: NEMATODA; COPEPODA; TURBELLARIA; GASTROTRICHA; POLYCHAETA; OSTRACODA. These are reported principal biomass contributors, not an exhaustive inventory.
